vikram: Quick summary from this morning's bakeoff running weight-only llm.int8 (bitsandbytes / llm.int8) on zephyr-12b-v1. Wanted to call out accuracy vs throughput tradeoffs we observed.

vikram: Setup: p4d.24xlarge (A100), CUDA 12, bnb 0.39, transformers patched to use llm.int8 path. Tests: TriviaQA emscore, MMLU subset, and a 2k-context latency sweep.

vikram: Command we used:
```
python bench/runner.py --model zephyr-12b-v1 --quant llmint8 --backend bitsandbytes --gpu a100 --batch 4 --seq 2048 --prompt-set triviaqa_sub --trials 3
```

ml-ci-bot: CI: reproduce job queued (job-id: 2026-ML-3387). Logs will be here: https://ci.redwood.dev/jobs/2026-ML-3387

vikram: Results (median across 3 runs):
- baseline fp16: p95 token latency = 85ms, throughput = 520 tok/s, TriviaQA accuracy = 68.2
- llm.int8 (bnb default w-only): p95 = 118ms (+39%), throughput = 360 tok/s (-31%), TriviaQA = 66.6 (-1.6 abs)
- llm.int8 tuned (grouping=64, disable_fastpath=false): p95 = 105ms, throughput = 420 tok/s, TriviaQA = 66.9 (-1.3 abs)

vikram: Perplexity-like proxy (logprob on heldout): fp16=2.14, llm.int8=2.22 (small degradation, consistent with QA drop).

sara: Thanks — interesting that throughput drops quite a bit. Any idea why p95 regressed so much vs fp16 but tuned path recovered some?

vikram: Hypothesis: bnb weight-only introduces extra kernel overhead + more KV cache memory churn for long context; grouping size controls IO pattern and reduces kernel launches. Also our batch concat path wasn't coalescing small requests well. Tuned grouping helped.

noah: Were all runs using same kv-cache strategy? iirc we had an optimization landed last week that avoids copying cache on 2k contexts for fp16 but not for int8. Could be that.

frankie: Can you paste the exact bnb init flags you used for the three runs?

vikram: Sure — defaults vs tuned:
- default: `bnb.init(quant_type=\"llm.int8\", use_double_quant=True, quant_backend=\"bitsandbytes\")`
- tuned: `bnb.init(quant_type=\"llm.int8\", use_double_quant=True, quant_backend=\"bitsandbytes\", group_size=64, threaded_kernels=True)`

vikram: Also tried 32 and 128 group_size: 32=slightly worse latency, 128=good throughput but +0.2 abs QA drop. So 64 is a decent middle ground for this model.

sara: What about memory footprint? Any chance we can fit larger batch if int8 is smaller?

vikram: Yes, peak GPU memory dropped ~18% vs fp16 which allowed +1 batch in some configs, but because of kernel overhead throughput still lower until we tuned grouping. For Zephyr12B at seq=2048: fp16 peak=38GB, llm.int8 peak=31GB.

noah: Could we try the llmint8 path but with mixed layers (first N layers fp16) as a canary? Might recover QA with moderate perf cost.

frankie: Agreed — propose a quick sweep: keep top 2 and bottom 2 layers fp16, rest int8. We should run on the same CI job and tag runs. I'll queue it after lunch.

vikram: Good plan. If that improves TriviaQA by >0.7 abs with <10% throughput loss vs tuned int8, we can include a fallback profile for Dedicated customers (latency-preferred vs cost-preferred).

ops-bot: deploy-bench: started instance p4d-2026-07-14-11:14 for follow-up sweep (run-id: 2026-BN-4421).

ml-ci-bot: Note: also add a regression alert for MMLU micro-slice we used (slice id: mm_micro_v2) if drop >1.0 abs next runs.

vikram: TL;DR: llm.int8 weight-only currently reduces memory significantly and saves cost but has non-trivial p95/throughput regression on zephyr-12b-v1 until grouping and kernel flags are tuned. QA drop ~1.3-1.8 abs — acceptable for some workloads, not for high-accuracy ones. Next steps: mixed-layer sweep (frankie), test kv-cache copy avoidance for int8 (noah), and prepare a short doc for product about two recommended profiles (cost-first tuned int8, latency-first mixed-layers).

sara: Sounds good. Please drop the run artifacts and a short table into the PR so infra/docs can grab numbers.

vikram: Will do — uploading bench artifacts to the job link and opening PR with results and suggested fallback profiles.

frankie: tagging @sara for product visibility :eyes:

noah: I'll look into the cache-copy path tonight.

vikram: thanks all.
